notes: Libretto by Emanuel Schikaneder (1791). Words as printed in the Edition Peters vocal score, which the app follows where it differs from the libretto: "und Sterbliche sind Göttern gleich" (the libretto has "den Göttern"), "Sie kommt" (the libretto has "kömmt"), "bei Seite" in two words, the Boys' "vor Gram vergehen" (the libretto has "für Gram"), Pamina's "Ha! des Jammers Maas ist voll!" (the libretto has "Ja, des Jammers Maß"), "Sieh Pamina stirbt durch dich!" without a comma, "tödte" in the old spelling and "er fühlet Gegenliebe" (the libretto has "fühlte"), the print's apostrophes ("Sonn'", "gold'ner", "steig'", "kehr'", "Erd'", "nah'", "geh'n", "seh'n", "Welch'", "sieh'", "halt'", "vollend'", "möcht'", "Müh'"), and the repeats of the music ("und Sterbliche sind Göttern gleich", "damit wir, was sie mache, seh'n", Pamina's "bald werden wir vermählet sein", "Mutter, Mutter!" and "ich möcht' ihn seh'n", "Komm, wir wollen zu ihm geh'n", "die Götter selbsten schützen sie"). In bar 14 the print has a full stop after the Third Boy's "Sonn'"; it is kept. "dunkle" is printed without a hyphen and is split dun-kle. Each Boy has his own line; the print puts two Boys on one staff in places, and Pamina on the First Boy's staff. IPA follows sung German stage diction: final -er, -ern as [ɐ]; the prefixes er-, ver-, zer- with [ɛr]; r elsewhere rolled or flipped; ch as [ç] after front vowels and [x] after back vowels; glottal stops [ʔ] before initial vowels; final b d g devoiced.
